body:
customer-ops: FYI customer reported 401s and intermittent TLS timeouts from their Private deployment. Started after they rotated service-account keys. Calls to our inference endpoint sometimes fail during handshake and sometimes return 401.

customer-ops: Payload from customer (sanitized):
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://inference.private.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to inference.private.redwood.example.com (10.0.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection to 10.0.5.12:443 (err=7)
* SSL: certificate verify failed (result:5)
* Closing connection 0
curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: certificate has expired
```

alex_support: Hmm. certificate verify failed + auth 401s could be two separate issues but they correlate. If TLS fails the client will often retry and then our auth exchange fails. Ask customer for `openssl s_client` output and an STUN of SNI.

customer-ops: They ran: `openssl s_client -connect inference.private.redwood.example.com:443 -servername inference.private.redwood.example.com` and got the chain back but with an intermediate missing (chain length 2) and the client shows `verify return:1` then `verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate`. They say it works from their laptop but not from app hosts in the VPC.

maria_infra: Sounds like return-path / ephemeral port rewrite issue. If the NAT or NACL is dropping packets mid-handshake the client will see handshake failures which can present like cert errors. Also possible their egress proxy (transparent TLS inspect) is swapping certs for hosts outside allowlist.

devon_networks: Quick checklist: 1) Are our control-plane IPs allowed in their egress allowlist? 2) Is there any TLS MITM / appliance in path? 3) Are security group rules stateful but NACLs stateless causing asymmetric flows?

alex_support: I asked customer to run reproducible curl from a bastion in same subnet and show `-v` plus `-I` and `--resolve` to bypass DNS. They sent back: 
```
curl -v --resolve inference.private.redwood.example.com:443:10.0.5.12 https://inference.private.redwood.example.com/v1/health -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
* Connected to 10.0.5.12 (10.0.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Encrypted Extensions (8)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Certificate (11)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, CERT verify (15)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Finished (20)
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Finished (20)
* SSL connection using TLSv1.3 / TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
> GET /v1/health HTTP/1.1
> Host: inference.private.redwood.example.com
> Authorization: Bearer <token>
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
```

customer-ops: So TLS succeeded from bastion but app hosts still get cert verify fails. They also provided `tcpdump` from app host which shows SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK, then server sends FIN immediately after ServerHello sometimes.

jess_sre: FIN after ServerHello indicates something midstream resetting session — could be a stateful firewall timeout/conntrack issue or a deep packet inspector rejecting the stream when it sees the cert chain. Do we have any firewall logs on their side?

customer-ops: They attached a NACL audit: ingress had a DENY for ephemeral range 49152-65535 explicitly, while outbound had ALLOW. They thought outbound allow was enough.

maria_infra: Yep that's the classic stateless NACL pitfall. NACLs are stateless so you must allow both directions for ephemeral ports. If inbound DENY exists for ephemeral, replies from our servers that use ephemeral ports for return will be dropped — causing the client to see handshake truncation or cert chain errors.

devon_networks: Also check if their NAT device is using port range remapping. If it remaps return ports into a different range that is DENYed by the NACL, you'll get asymmetric flows.

alex_support: I pushed a quick repro doc to them: 1) From app host run `curl -v` while tcpdump on server side shows missing TCP segments. 2) Temporarily add an ALLOW inbound NACL rule for 1024-65535 to test. 3) Confirm client no longer sees SSL verify failures.

customer-ops: They did the inbound ALLOW for ephemeral and reported immediate improvement: TLS handshakes stable and 401 errors gone. Said `:party:`

jess_sre: Great. Root cause: customer's NACL had asymmetric rules blocking ephemeral return ports so TLS handshakes were intermittently torn down. That caused retries to hit partial auth flows -> 401s.

maria_infra: Action items: - Recommend they add symmetric allow for ephemeral ports (1024-65535) on NACLs and ensure SGs allow ephemeral returns (SGs are stateful but good to check). - Check any TLS-inspect appliances for cert substitution on app hosts (they had one but it was bypassed on bastion). - We'll add KB entry about NACL asymmetric ephemeral blocking causing TLS/auth weirdness.

devon_networks: Also advised customer to pin our control-plane and runtime IP ranges in their allowlist and to avoid port-range deny rules that are narrower than NAT translations.

alex_support: I'll follow up in case they want a postmortem/KB. Good catch team. :thumbsup:
thread_summary: Customer experienced TLS handshake truncation and 401s due to asymmetric NACL rules blocking ephemeral return ports. Repro steps, tcpdump and openssl diagnostics led to inbound ephemeral range allow fix; recommended KB and symmetric NACL rules.
